content.comment_body: I have two systems running [product_name] devices. After upgrading my Mac, I can only find a demo version download link. Previously, I had the software installed on my old Mac and used it for development, but that’s no longer accessible. My devices originally came with a CD, but there's no registration code and my Mac lacks a CD drive. How can I obtain the full version now?

You can either borrow or purchase a USB drive, or copy the CD to a USB stick using another computer since your Mac has no CD drive. Then, follow the instructions in this FAQ: 'How do you install a downloaded upgrade for [product_name] with or without the software already installed?' You may download the upgrade to [product_name] [version_no] free of charge. Note that it is a complete package of approximately 1.3 GB.

analysis.insight_summary: Users transitioning to new Macs encounter challenges reinstalling the full version of [product_name], often finding only demo versions available and lacking a registration code. The inability to use the original CD due to missing hardware, such as CD drives, demonstrates how changes in hardware and software distribution impact user experience. Although downloading an upgrade package is possible, users often lack guidance on licensing or access to the full version, complicating the process.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect a straightforward method to reinstall the full version of [product_name] on a new device, preferably via a direct download and recognition of prior ownership—without the need for extra hardware or complex steps.
